stages.name: Get Active ATS Registry
stages.note: Reads which job boards to poll (Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby/Recruitee/Workable) - this registry is itself written by the discovery stage, which recognizes known ATS board URL patterns and adds a row per company+board it finds.

stages.name: Poll Each Registry Row
stages.note: Per-registry-row batching, same isolation principle as every other stage in this pipeline - one board's API hiccup can't abort the rest of the poll.

stages.name: Compute Diff
stages.note: The actual point of this workflow: classifies each posting as new / still-open / closed by diffing the board's current listing against what the database already has open. New postings get inserted, still-open postings just get a freshness timestamp bump, and postings that disappeared from the board get closed.

stages.name: Has Upserts? -> Bulk Upsert Current Jobs
Has Closed Jobs? -> Close Missing Jobs
Update Registry Success / Handle Failure -> Update Registry Failure
stages.note: Per-row success/failure is tracked on the registry itself, not just logged globally - a board that's been failing for a while is visible at the registry level, not buried in a run log.

stages.name: Get Updated Source Stats -> Update Source Stats Sheet Row -> Increment Row Stats

why_this_exists: TheirStack Discovery (the weekly seed stage) only tells you a posting existed the day it searched. Without this stage, a posting closed the day after discovery would stay 'open' in the database for up to a week until the next weekly TheirStack run - which means Scoring would keep awarding 'stale posting' points to a company that already filled the role. ATS Poller closes that gap daily by going straight to the source board (Greenhouse/Lever/etc.) rather than waiting on the next weekly discovery pass.
